extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / New York Times readership (1929)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and brief stylistic/layout rules implied on a 1929 New York Times newspaper page for presenting news (editorial motto and page-design remarks). Useful for front-page/news-homepage composition and layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper editorial motto / selection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "All the News That's Fit to Print." — The New York Times (Elements of Journalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the paper's stated editorial standard for newsworthiness; presented as the guiding slogan/copyright line ("Copyright, 1929, by The New York Times Company."). No further elaboration on selection criteria is printed on the page, but the motto functions as the overarching principle for what the paper chooses to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page layout: use of boxes and heads to relieve monotony
rubrics_metrics.description: "The effect is achieved through the regular arrangement of boxes and heads. Monotony of too much solid body is relieved by the two heads at the bottom of the page."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design guidance for front-page composition: arrange content in boxes and use headline 'heads' to break up large blocks of body text; place additional heads (subheads) at lower page positions to prevent visual monotony. Implies balancing text density with typographic elements for readable, visually engaging pages.
